title: Text Transform preset 13: fan out (the bottom edge drawn in)
description: HHHHHHH in Lato Bold, 10 mm, centred at (50, 50) mm, with Text Transform preset 13 (fan out): every letter keeps its height, its top corners stay on the straight text and its bottom corners draw in towards the centre, the bottom edge being the straight text scaled by 0.70 about its centre. OpenStitch fits the two edges from the letters' corners in tools/fit_envelopes.py.

evidence.note: compat/reference/text/text-transform-13.pes, PE-DESIGN 11.50 (pe-gui): box 12.3..87.7 x 39.7..50.0 mm; letter bottoms at 23.9..30.0 (first) to 70.0..76.3 mm (last), tops at the straight positions.

Stitch count not checked, as in the other Text Transform specs: OpenStitch sews 1653 stitches to PE-DESIGN's 1171 (+41 %; +14 % on the straight-edged presets), the text fill's row structure (audit, 'Text fill rows'), not the envelope. The sheared stems have no vertical columns to measure; the letters' corners are checked in the unit test text_transform_presets_warp_the_straight_text.

references.make: On a 100 × 100 mm Design Page (File > New), with Lato Bold (crates/openstitch-design/fonts/Lato-Bold.ttf, OFL) installed for the current Windows user and used as a TrueType font. Text tool, click at (50, 50) mm and type HHHHHHH: Lato, size 10.0 mm, alignment Center, region Fill Stitch in 800 RED with the text's own Sewing Attributes (under sewing off, density 5.0), line Not Sewn. Text Attributes > Transform on, preset 13 of the palette in reading order (the two arches first, then the grid row by row). Keep the text inside the page. Save As PES (default type) as compat/reference/text/text-transform-13.pes and record in compat/reference/MANIFEST.json the PE-DESIGN version, date, OS, the font as PE lists it, the preset and its box (see docs/COMPATIBILITY_TESTS.md).
